thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Slip On Concerns of New Conflict in Middle East

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Slip On Concerns of New Conflict in Middle East
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Monday's regular session:
VelocityShares Daily 2x VIX Short Term ETN ( TVIX ): -1.5%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.1%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.2%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.3%
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): -1.8%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including SPY, IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was down 0.7%.
U.S. stocks turned negative at session's half after the Israeli prime minister re-ignited worries over conflict in the Mideast.
Earlier, equities logged gains fueled by a barrage of mergers -- including Sprint's (S) merger with T-Mobile (TMUS), the $35.6 billion acquisition of Andeavor (ANDV) by Marathon (MRO), and Marriott Vacation's (VAC) acquisition of ILG (ILG). -- as well as upbeat earnings from McDonald's and Allergan (AGN).
A miss on the pending home sales index (+0.4% vs +1.0% estimates) coupled with reports Israel closed its airspace with Syria prompted the first pull-back in stocks. Shares retreated a second time after Israel prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Iran has moved its nuclear stockpiles to secret locations.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 0.6% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were lower.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 1.9% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was down 1.2%.
Apple (AAPL) rose nearly 2% after media reports said the company is considering a significant cash return to shareholders over the next several years to offset the growing disappointment over sales of the iPhone X. According to the UK Times, the company is considering whether to announce this week a plan to give shareholders as much as $400 billion in dividends and stock buybacks in the next two to three years. A buyback has been made more likely by President Donald Trump's tax cuts, which will allow Apple to repatriate its $252 billion foreign cash pile without an enormous capital gains tax bill, the Times said.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.1%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 0.5% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 0.5%..
CNA Financial (CNA) rose more than 3% after the firm reported Q1 adjusted earnings of $1.03 per share, up from $0.87 in the same period a year ago and exceeding the estimate of $0.91 from analysts polled by CapIQ. Total revenue of $1.81 billion was up from $1.63 billion in the same period a year ago and topped the Street projection of $1.80 billion. CNA maintained its quarterly dividend of $0.30 per share. The dividend is payable May 30to stockholders of record on May 14.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 0.4% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.4%.
Oil production companies Marathon Petroleum (MPC) and Andeavor (ANDV) have agreed to merge in a deal which will see Marathon acquire Andeavor's shares for a total equity value of $23.3 billion or a total enterprise value of $35.6 billion. Marathon said that the transaction would generate approximately $1 billion of tangible annual run-rate synergies within the first three years while "significantly enhancing" its long-term cash flow generation profile. The combination is also expected to diversify its refining portfolio geographically, increase access to advantaged feedstocks and enhance its midstream footprint in the Permian basin. Under the terms of the deal, Andeavor shareholders will have the option to choose 1.87 shares of Marathon stock, or $152.27 in cash subject to a proration mechanism which will result in 15% of Andeavor's fully diluted shares receiving cash consideration. Marathon and Andeavor shareholders will then own approximately 66% and 34% of the combined company, respectively. MPC shares fell more than 7% and ANDV shares jumped more than 13%.
Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) fell 0.5% and other industrial funds Vanguard Industrials (VIS) and iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ), were in the red.
AK Steel (AKS) were more than 5% lower after the steelmaker reported Q1 earnings and revenues above expectations compiled by Capital IQ. Q1 EPS was $0.09, down from $0.26 per share a year earlier but better than expectations for a loss of $0.01 a share. Revenues rose to $1.66 billion from $1.53 billion and beat the $1.58 billion mean estimate. Looking ahead, the company expects market conditions to strengthen in Q2 compared to Q1. It expects flat-rolled shipments in Q2 to be 5% to 7% higher on a sequential basis.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.3%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 0.5%. Natural gas was down 1.2% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 1.2%.
Gold was down 0.4%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.5%. Silver was down 0.7%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 1.1%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 0.3% and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were firmer.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 0.01% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were in negative territory.
Walmart (WMT) agreed to merge its UK unit, Asda, the third largest grocer in the UK, with J Sainsbury, the second largest, in a cash and share transaction, to better compete with German discount supermarket chains Aldi and Lidl and e-commerce giant Amazon.com (AMZN). Under the terms of the merger, which values Asda at GBP 7.3 billion ($10.04 billion), Walmart will hold 42% of the combination and will receive about GBP2.98 billion in cash, the Brentonville, Arkansas-based company said on Monday in a statement. This holding will be made up of 29.9% of Sainsbury shares, with full voting rights, with the balance held as non-voting shares convertible into voting shares. The deal is subject to various approvals, including from the UK antitrust watchdog, the Competition and Markets Authority. The companies plan to maintain both the Sainsbury's and Asda brands and they don't plan any store closures. Getting all the approvals could extend into H2 2019. WMT shares were up 1.2%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.01% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were higher. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 1.5%.
Pluristem Therapeutics (PSTI) shares rose more than 8% after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the company's investigational new drug (IND) application for PLX-R18 cell therapy for the treatment of acute radiation syndrome (ARS). By approving the IND, Pluristem can treat victims who may have been acutely exposed to high dose radiation due to nuclear attack or accident and can start the necessary preparations in order to keep an emergency stock of PLX-R18 ready for use in such events. Pluristem is currently in discussions with the FDA and several U.S. governmental agencies, including the Department of Defense, to clear the path for its proposed pivotal study of PLX-R18 in ARS.
